label: Political science
learning_takeaway: Examine how rules and participants' choices shape collective decisions involving government.
support_note: The textbook defines political science's focus and an analytical framework.

label: Constitution (politics)
learning_takeaway: Understand how basic rules assign governmental powers, duties and limits.
support_note: The source distinguishes constitutional functions from whether they occupy one document.

label: Parliamentary sovereignty
locator: Opening and Developments affecting Parliamentary sovereignty
learning_takeaway: Explore Parliament's legal supremacy in the UK and its relationship with institutional reforms.
support_note: The explanation distinguishes constitutional principle from laws Parliament may repeal.

label: Uncodified constitution
locator: Parliamentary sovereignty and the UK constitution
learning_takeaway: Distinguish lacking a single constitutional document from lacking written constitutional rules.
support_note: Parliament describes the UK's constitution as partly written and wholly uncodified.

label: Parliament Act 1911
locator: Why were the Parliament Acts brought into force?
learning_takeaway: Connect the 1909 budget conflict with replacing most Lords vetoes by delay.
support_note: The account identifies the remaining exception and later 1949 reduction.

label: Salisbury convention
learning_takeaway: Explore restraint by the Lords toward government bills promised in an election manifesto.
support_note: The convention concerns not voting down manifesto bills.

label: Money bills under the Parliament Acts
locator: Bills subject to the Parliament Acts
learning_takeaway: Compare the Lords' restricted role over money bills with other public bills.
support_note: The page describes Commons origin and the one-month procedure.

label: Bicameralism
locator: Opening and Bills subject to the Parliament Acts
learning_takeaway: Understand two-chamber lawmaking through the qualified Commons–Lords example.
support_note: Both houses normally pass bills, with explicitly described exceptions.

label: Mixed-member proportional representation
locator: Two votes; electorate MPs and list MPs
learning_takeaway: See how constituency representation combines with a party-proportional seat total.
support_note: The official New Zealand explanation separates party and electorate votes.

label: New Zealand MMP threshold
locator: Political parties try to win party votes and electorate votes
learning_takeaway: Explore two alternative routes to eligibility for proportional representation.
support_note: The stated threshold is five percent of party votes or one electorate win.

label: Confidence and supply agreement
locator: Parties negotiate to form a government
learning_takeaway: Distinguish supporting a government on specified matters from joining its coalition.
support_note: The electoral authority lists both as different possible interparty arrangements.

label: Constructive vote of no confidence
learning_takeaway: Understand why Germany requires choosing a successor while removing the Chancellor.
support_note: A majority election of the successor is the constitutional condition.

label: German eternity clause
learning_takeaway: Distinguish a difficult amendment from a constitutionally inadmissible amendment.
support_note: Some protected principles remain beyond the two-thirds amendment procedure.

label: Concurrent legislative powers in Germany
learning_takeaway: See how federal action can displace state legislative authority within a shared competence.
support_note: Article 72 allows Länder action while the Federation has not legislated.

label: Standing to sue
learning_takeaway: Distinguish a concrete, redressable legal injury from disagreement with government policy.
support_note: The federal test connects injury, causation and redressability.

label: Amicus curiae
learning_takeaway: Understand how a nonparty can contribute a brief to a court's consideration.
support_note: Participation is governed by court-specific rules rather than party status.

label: Rule of lenity
learning_takeaway: Explore construing unresolved criminal-law ambiguity in a defendant's favor.
support_note: The explanation connects the principle with legislative responsibility for defining crimes.

label: Habeas corpus
learning_takeaway: Distinguish judicial review of detention's lawfulness from an ordinary new criminal trial.
support_note: The writ brings custody under court review through a civil petition.

label: Stare decisis
learning_takeaway: Compare following a higher court with following one's own prior decisions.
support_note: The doctrine promotes consistency but is not an absolute bar to overruling.

label: Burden of proof
learning_takeaway: Compare who must prove a proposition with how much proof the proceeding requires.
support_note: The entry contrasts most civil cases with criminal guilt and notes exceptions.

label: Summary judgment
learning_takeaway: Understand deciding a claim without trial when no material factual dispute requires resolution.
support_note: The moving party must also be entitled to judgment as a matter of law.

label: Preliminary injunction
learning_takeaway: Explore temporary relief before final judgment and why irreparable harm matters.
support_note: The entry identifies merits, harm, equities and public-interest considerations.

label: Claim preclusion
learning_takeaway: Understand why a resolved cause of action generally cannot be litigated again.
support_note: Finality can bind a losing party or prevent additional recovery by a winner.

label: Issue preclusion
learning_takeaway: Distinguish relitigating a decided issue from repeating an entire claim.
support_note: The issue must have been validly, finally and necessarily determined.

label: Citizens' assemblies
locator: How does the Citizens' Assembly work?; recommendations
learning_takeaway: Explore informed public deliberation whose recommendations remain advisory in Ireland.
support_note: The official account distinguishes evidence, small-group deliberation and legislative authority.

label: Stratified sortition for citizens’ assemblies
locator: How are members selected?; recruitment method
learning_takeaway: See how lottery recruitment and demographic stratification produce an intended mini-public.
support_note: Random household invitations precede stratified selection from applicants.

label: Regulatory sandbox
locator: What the Regulatory Sandbox offers; tests; tools
learning_takeaway: Distinguish supervised, limited testing from exemption from regulation.
support_note: The FCA retains authorization requirements and cannot waive national or international law.

label: Freedom of Information Act (United States)
locator: What is the FOIA?; What can I ask for?
learning_takeaway: Understand access to existing federal agency records subject to specified exemptions.
support_note: Agencies generally disclose records but need not create research or new records.

label: FOIA segregability
learning_takeaway: See why an exempt passage need not justify withholding the entire record.
support_note: The statute requires reasonable segregation and release of nonexempt information.

label: Government in the Sunshine Act
learning_takeaway: Explore public observation of covered federal agency meetings and formal closure procedures.
support_note: The statute defines covered collegial bodies and provides specific exceptions and recorded votes.

label: Sunset provision
learning_takeaway: Understand automatic expiration as a way to require renewed legislative approval.
support_note: The example terminates a program unless legislators review and renew it.

label: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission
learning_takeaway: Compare truth-finding, reparations and amnesty as separate parts of a post-apartheid process.
support_note: The official account identifies the three committees and their distinct mandates.

label: Conditional amnesty in South Africa's TRC
locator: 18 August 1997 statement; Khanyile and Tumahole decisions
learning_takeaway: See why political context alone did not guarantee amnesty without full disclosure.
support_note: The same statement records denial for nondisclosure and grants for politically associated acts.

label: Brown v. Board of Education
locator: Brown v. Board of Education case summary
learning_takeaway: Explore the constitutional rejection of state-mandated racial segregation in public education.
support_note: The Court found segregated educational facilities inherently unequal under equal protection.

label: Gideon v. Wainwright
learning_takeaway: Connect an indigent defendant's denied lawyer with the right to appointed counsel in state felony trials.
support_note: The case applies the Sixth Amendment guarantee through Fourteenth Amendment due process.
